$comment: RECORDED DEFECT COUNTS FOR THE ASYNCAPI CONTRACT. Read by contract_lint.py, which fails
when any count MOVES — up or down. Seeded 2026-09-09 against
api/mqtt/schema/iotc-rfd40-90-mqtt.asyncapi.json at info.version 1.26.0.
THIS FILE IS NOT AN ALLOWLIST, and the distinction matters. It suppresses nothing: every
finding is still printed by `--report`, and there is no way to silence an individual one.
It records a COUNT, so the gate's question is not 'is the contract clean' — it plainly is
not — but 'did the incoming drop introduce a NEW defect of a class we can already detect'.
WHY A COUNT RATHER THAN ZERO. The contract must never be edited from this repository. A
zero-threshold gate would therefore be permanently red on 311 findings nobody here is
allowed to fix, and validate.yml already records what happens then: a gate that checks a
thing nobody is permitted to fix gets deactivated. A gate born red is a gate born ignored.
A COUNT THAT GOES DOWN IS ALSO A FAILURE. That is deliberate and it is not pedantry: the
moment a defect is fixed upstream, the number here becomes a false claim about the
contract, and a stale baseline is how a gate stops meaning anything. Lower it in the same
commit that observes the fix, and say so in the message.
WHAT EACH COUNT MEANS
unresolvable_refs           An internal $ref pointing at a node that is not there. The
one hard-defect class here, and the document is CLEAN — so
this is the check most worth having: it is the only one whose
baseline is 0, and any movement is unambiguous.
provenance_dangling         A schema file named ANYWHERE in the contract that is not in
this repository — x-iotc-provenance, description or summary.
530 dangling citations: the whole provenance layer points at
the pre-AsyncAPI schema tree deleted at c4d7de7c, across 49
distinct filenames. Filed as schema-issues-2026-09-08.md 2.8
/ summary row 20.
review_state_in_description Review, decision or SELF-CITATION state inside a published
gloss — a description or an example summary. 'IS CLOSED',
'PREMISE WAS WRONG', 'UNRESOLVED', a sentence quoting what
'the API reference states', or a back-link naming the label
the reference site publishes. All of them invert the direction
of authority: the statement of truth deferring to its own
generated output. Filed as 4.12 / rows 21, 22 and 23.
constraint_only_in_prose    A numeric limit that exists in a description and in no
keyword, so no consumer can enforce it and no validator can
see it. Includes limits that are asserted, retired, or
declared-but-unenforced — the check does not try to tell them
apart, because distinguishing them means reading prose.
Overlaps 4.2, 4.6 and 4.10.
RE-SEEDED 2026-09-09 (b). TWO COUNTS MOVED AND THE CONTRACT DID NOT CHANGE. This is the
one case the rule above does not cover, so it is recorded here rather than left for
somebody to reverse-engineer from a diff. Both checks were widened, not added:
provenance_dangling         230 -> 530.  The check read x-iotc-provenance ONLY. That is a
MACHINE field: nothing publishes it, so a dangling name there
is hygiene. The same dead filenames also sit in `description`
(296) and `summary` (4), which the generator CAN put in front
of a reader — so the citations that actually reach a page were
the ones the check could not see.
review_state_in_description 70 -> 200.  The check read `description` ONLY, and its marker
set matched none of the 86 `Also published as "<label>"`
back-links or the 81 summaries that are nothing but a citation
of the site generated FROM this contract. The key tuple and the
marker set had to widen TOGETHER; either alone finds nothing.
THE DECOMPOSITION IS EXACT, AND IT IS THE PROOF THAT THIS IS INSTRUMENT AND NOT DRIFT.
Neither pre-existing column moved by one: 530 = 230 (x-iotc-provenance, unchanged) + 296
+ 4, and 200 = 70 (description with the old markers, unchanged) + 130 (summary with the new
markers), with ZERO overlap between the old and new marker sets. Re-derive both splits with
`python3 scripts/api/mqtt/contract_lint.py --report` and group the pointers by their last
key. If a future drop moves either count, it has moved the contract.
TO RAISE THESE UPSTREAM: `python3 scripts/api/mqtt/contract_lint.py --report` prints every
finding with its RFC 6901 pointer, and exits 0 so it can be piped into an issue body.
LOWERED 2026-09-22. THE CONTRACT CHANGED, AND ALL THREE MOVES ARE FIXES. The 2026-09-21
rebuild (still info.version 1.26.0) takes every payload schema, field and example from the
IoT Connector API definition (openapi.json and the files it references), so the commentary
these checks were counting went with the schemas that carried it:
constraint_only_in_prose    11 -> 0.
review_state_in_description 200 -> 0.
provenance_dangling         530 -> 102. None of the 102 is the deleted pre-AsyncAPI tree
any more. Each is the contract naming the API definition's
own files -- openapi.json (52) and the command, response and
event file behind each message (50) -- which live in the
IOTC_APIS repository, not in this one. They are provenance,
not dangling links, but the check cannot tell the difference,
so the count is recorded rather than worked around. A drop
that renames or drops one of those citations moves it.
